title: System.Text.Json Source Generation
description: Improve serialization performance with System.Text.Json source-generated serializers.

data.text: `System.Text.Json` source generation moves JSON serialization logic to compile time. This eliminates reflection at runtime and dramatically improves serialization speed and startup time.
Define a partial class with `JsonSerializerContext` and mark it with `[JsonSerializable]` for each type you want to serialize.

data.title: Define a JsonSerializerContext

data.text: Source-generated serializers are required for Native AOT because reflection-based serializers cannot be trimmed.

terms.definition: A partial class that holds source-generated serializers for specific types.
An attribute that registers a type for source-generated serialization.
Ahead-of-time compilation, which requires source generation for JSON.

data.title: Important
data.text: Source generation is the only option for JSON serialization in Native AOT apps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Source generation removes runtime reflection overhead.
Required for Native AOT and useful for high-performance apps.
data.takeaway: System.Text.Json source generation is the future of fast JSON serialization in .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Create a Source-Generated Serializer
data.description: Add source-generated JSON serialization to an existing model.
steps: Add `[JsonSerializable]` for WeatherForecast and its array type.
Serialize and deserialize using the generated context.
Measure startup time with BenchmarkDotNet if time allows.
data.expectedOutcome: You can serialize types without reflection using source generation.
